subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a short piece of a class discussion. Read the turns of talk and answer the question about what makes a good discussion: which reply stays on topic, which question is relevant, which speaker is following the rules, and which statement is clear. Everything you need is right in the item.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Should the school start a recycling club? MIA: I think we should, because we throw away a lot of paper every day. Which reply by Ben stays on topic and responds to Mia? A) A recycling club could collect that paper and turn it into something useful. B) My favorite color is green. C) I forgot my lunch money today. Write the letter and the reply that stays on topic.
items.answer: A) A recycling club could collect that paper and turn it into something useful.

steps: The topic is starting a recycling club, and Mia gave a reason about wasted paper.
An on-topic reply must connect to recycling and to Mia's point about paper.
Choice A talks about collecting the paper Mia mentioned, so it stays on topic and responds to her.
Choices B and C change the subject to color and lunch money, which have nothing to do with the discussion.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Was the main character brave? LEO: The article says he climbed the cliff to save the dog. Which question best invites the group to keep talking about Leo's idea? A) What time is it? B) What other moments in the article show whether he was brave? C) Do you like dogs? Write the letter and the best question.
items.answer: B) What other moments in the article show whether he was brave?

steps: A good discussion question connects to what the speaker just said and asks the group to add more.
Leo pointed to evidence from the article about bravery, so the best question keeps the group looking at the article.
Choice B asks for more moments about bravery, which builds directly on Leo's point.
Choices A and C are off topic and would end the discussion instead of moving it forward.

items.prompt: Read the rule and the situation. RULE: Everyone must point to a detail from the text before sharing an opinion. SARA says: I just think the ending is happy. Did Sara follow the rule? A) Yes, because she shared an opinion. B) No, because she did not point to any detail from the text. C) Yes, because she spoke politely. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: B) No, because she did not point to any detail from the text.

steps: The agreed-upon rule says a speaker must point to a detail from the text before sharing an opinion.
Sara only gave her opinion that the ending is happy and did not name any detail from the text.
Choice B is correct because she skipped the required step of using a text detail.
Choices A and C ignore the rule; sharing an opinion or being polite does not meet the requirement to cite a detail.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Should students get more time for lunch? KIM: Ten more minutes would let us finish eating and relax. JON: My uncle drives a truck. Which speaker did not contribute to the discussion, and why? A) Kim, because she gave a reason. B) Jon, because his comment is off topic and does not respond to Kim. C) Neither, because both stayed on topic. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: B) Jon, because his comment is off topic and does not respond to Kim.

steps: The topic is whether students should get more lunch time.
Kim contributed by giving a clear reason about finishing eating and relaxing.
Jon's comment about his uncle driving a truck has nothing to do with lunch time and does not respond to Kim.
Choice B is correct; an off-topic comment that ignores the speaker is not an effective contribution.

items.prompt: Read this turn. TARA: It is just bad, you know? Which revision states Tara's idea most clearly for a discussion? A) It is so bad, really bad. B) I think the new seating plan is unfair because it splits up friends who help each other study. C) Bad, very bad, you know? Write the letter and the clearest version.
items.answer: B) I think the new seating plan is unfair because it splits up friends who help each other study.

steps: A clear contribution states a claim and gives a reason in complete language.
Tara's original turn is vague because it does not say what is bad or why.
Choice B names the seating plan as unfair and gives a reason, so it is clear and complete.
Choices A and C only repeat the vague word bad and still do not explain Tara's idea.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Should the class read a mystery next? DAN: I vote yes, because mysteries keep me guessing until the end. Which reply by Eva builds on Dan's idea by adding a new reason? A) Yes, I agree, mysteries keep you guessing. B) Yes, and mysteries also teach us to notice small clues we might miss. C) I like pizza. Write the letter and the reply that adds a new reason.
items.answer: B) Yes, and mysteries also teach us to notice small clues we might miss.

steps: Building on an idea means adding a new reason or detail, not just repeating it.
Dan said mysteries keep him guessing, so a build adds a different reason to read mysteries.
Choice B agrees and then adds a new reason about noticing clues, which extends Dan's point.
Choice A only restates Dan's reason, and Choice C is off topic, so neither builds on the idea.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. ROSA: The story takes place during a snowstorm. NICK: Wait, can you say more about how the snowstorm changes the plan? Which best describes what Nick did? A) He asked a question that responds to Rosa and asks her to explain more. B) He changed the subject. C) He repeated exactly what Rosa said. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: A) He asked a question that responds to Rosa and asks her to explain more.

steps: Responding to a question or comment means connecting to what the speaker said.
Rosa mentioned the snowstorm, and Nick asked her to explain how it changes the plan.
Choice A is correct because Nick's question stays on Rosa's point and invites her to elaborate.
Choice B is wrong because he did not change the subject, and Choice C is wrong because he asked something new instead of repeating her.

items.prompt: Read the rule and the situation. RULE: Take turns and let one person finish before the next person speaks. During the discussion, PETE keeps interrupting before others finish their sentences. Is Pete following the rule? A) Yes, because he is excited. B) No, because he interrupts before others finish. C) Yes, because he has good ideas. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: B) No, because he interrupts before others finish.

steps: The rule asks speakers to take turns and let each person finish before the next one speaks.
Pete keeps interrupting before others finish their sentences.
Choice B is correct because interrupting breaks the turn-taking rule.
Choices A and C do not matter to this rule; being excited or having good ideas does not excuse interrupting.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Was the field trip a success? AMY: Yes, because we got to see real fossils up close. Which reply by Sam stays on topic and responds to Amy? A) Seeing the fossils helped me understand the chapter we read about dinosaurs. B) I want a new bike. C) The bus was blue. Write the letter and the on-topic reply.
items.answer: A) Seeing the fossils helped me understand the chapter we read about dinosaurs.

steps: The topic is whether the field trip was a success, and Amy gave a reason about seeing fossils.
An on-topic reply connects to the fossils and the value of the trip.
Choice A connects the fossils to understanding a chapter, which responds to Amy and stays on topic.
Choices B and C are off topic because wanting a bike and naming the bus color do not respond to whether the trip was a success.

items.prompt: Read this turn. JESS: Stuff happened. Which revision states Jess's idea most clearly for a discussion? A) Lots of stuff happened, really. B) Things happened, you know. C) I think the hero changed because she learned to trust her friends after the fire. Write the letter and the clearest version.
items.answer: C) I think the hero changed because she learned to trust her friends after the fire.

steps: A clear contribution gives a specific claim with a reason in complete language.
Jess's original turn is vague because stuff happened does not tell what happened or why it matters.
Choice C names what changed about the hero and gives a reason, so it is clear and complete.
Choices A and B just repeat vague words like stuff and things and still explain nothing.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. MARK: The poem repeats the word home three times. Which question best invites the group to keep talking about Mark's idea? A) Why do you think the poet repeats the word home? B) What is your favorite snack? C) Are we done yet? Write the letter and the best question.
items.answer: A) Why do you think the poet repeats the word home?

steps: A good discussion question connects to the speaker and asks the group to think more deeply.
Mark noticed that the word home is repeated, so the best question explores why.
Choice A asks the group to think about the reason for the repetition Mark noticed, which moves the discussion forward.
Choices B and C are off topic and would end the conversation instead of building on Mark's observation.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Should homework be shorter? GINA: Yes, because shorter homework gives us time to read for fun. TODD: I scored a goal in soccer. Which speaker did not contribute to the discussion, and why? A) Gina, because she gave an opinion. B) Todd, because his comment is off topic and ignores Gina. C) Neither, because both contributed. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: B) Todd, because his comment is off topic and ignores Gina.

steps: The topic is whether homework should be shorter.
Gina contributed with a reason about having time to read for fun.
Todd's comment about scoring a goal has nothing to do with homework and does not respond to Gina.
Choice B is correct because an off-topic comment that ignores the speaker is not an effective contribution.

items.prompt: Read the rule and the situation. RULE: Listen to the speaker and respond to what they actually said. ANA says: I think the rule about phones is too strict. BEN replies: That has nothing to do with anything, let me talk about the weather. Did Ben follow the rule? A) No, because he ignored Ana and changed the subject. B) Yes, because he spoke next. C) Yes, because he raised his hand first. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: A) No, because he ignored Ana and changed the subject.

steps: The rule says to listen to the speaker and respond to what they actually said.
Ana shared an opinion about the phone rule, but Ben switched to the weather instead of responding to her.
Choice A is correct because ignoring Ana and changing the subject breaks the rule.
Choices B and C are wrong; simply speaking next or raising a hand does not mean Ben responded to Ana's idea.

items.prompt: Read this exchange. TOPIC: Should the class plant a garden? OMAR: Yes, because a garden could grow vegetables for the food drive. Which reply by Lily builds on Omar's idea by adding a new reason? A) Yes, a garden could grow vegetables for the food drive. B) Yes, and taking care of it would also teach us responsibility. C) My shoes are new. Write the letter and the reply that adds a new reason.
items.answer: B) Yes, and taking care of it would also teach us responsibility.

steps: Building on an idea means adding a new reason or detail rather than repeating it.
Omar gave one reason, that a garden could grow vegetables for the food drive.
Choice B agrees and adds a different reason about learning responsibility, so it extends Omar's point.
Choice A only restates Omar's reason, and Choice C is off topic, so neither builds on the idea.

items.prompt: Read the rule and the situation. RULE: Point to a detail from the text before giving your opinion. RAJ says: I think the wolf is the hero because the text says he shared his food with the hungry rabbits. Did Raj follow the rule? A) No, because he gave an opinion. B) Yes, because he pointed to a detail from the text before his opinion. C) No, because opinions are not allowed. Write the letter and your answer.
items.answer: B) Yes, because he pointed to a detail from the text before his opinion.

steps: The rule says a speaker must point to a detail from the text before giving an opinion.
Raj gave the opinion that the wolf is the hero and supported it with the detail that the wolf shared his food with the rabbits.
Choice B is correct because Raj included a specific text detail to back up his opinion.
Choices A and C are wrong; giving an opinion is allowed as long as a text detail supports it, which Raj did.
